fact_label: Digital Nomad Visa (Visa V) age gate
Digital Nomad Visa (Visa V) documentation shape
value_raw: Official bank-issued statements for the last 3-6 months, each month individually clearing the income threshold (a strict no-averaging standard); an employment letter that explicitly states the work is remote (or foreign-client contracts / foreign business registration for freelancers and business owners); a Hague Apostille on supporting documents (notarization alone is not accepted); and a mandatory all-risk health policy covering the full visa duration including medical repatriation — ordinary travel insurance and Colombian public-health enrollment (EPS) both fail this test under 2026 practice.

Proof of a verifiable lifetime pension at the required level — a Social Security award, government or employer pension certification, or documented IRA/401(k) systematic-withdrawal arrangement. Ordinary investment, dividend, or rental income that is not structured as a pension or retirement-account withdrawal is the unresolved edge: the held record's own read is that it likely does not count cleanly, so income structured that way needs professional confirmation before relying on this route.

Bank statements evidencing the stable passive income at the required level, plus the underlying source documents themselves — rental contracts, dividend or annuity statements, or investment-account records. Passive income is this route's entire qualifying basis, so the documentation burden is proving the income stream's stability and origin, not proving employment.

Documentary proof of the qualifying investment (property deed or company-share/financial-asset records at the required level), plus a mandatory central-bank step no applicant can skip: the invested funds must be registered with Colombia's central bank (Banco de la República) on its foreign-exchange Form 4 before the visa application can proceed — transferring money and buying an asset is not by itself sufficient.
